Title: Motion (*.mtn) Open/Save
Content: Objective Motion is a native file format (*mtn) of Marvelous Designer that saves Avatar movement information, and is used when recording Animation of Garments and Avatars. Marvelous Designer provides Motion files for its default male and female Avatars, but Animation Data or Motion capture Data from third-party 3D solutions can be imported as COLLADA files, then extracted as a Motion file (*mtn) through this menu. Location Open Motion Main Menu File Open Joint Motion Save Motion Main Menu File Save As Joint Motion Operation Open Motion Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Joint Motion The Open File window appears. Navigate to the desired *mtn file, then click Open. The Load Motion Type window appears. Select from the available settings: Joint Information Joint Rotation &amp Translation Applies the Avatar's Height, Pose, Motion Data (Joint rotation,) and Joint positions Joint Rotation Only Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Garment Position Move Avatar &amp Garment to Start Position Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver 2.5.0). Transition Animation A transition Animation is an Animation that changes from a T-Pose to a motion's first Pose in stages, and is created when the Avatar's current Pose and Motion differs from that of the first frame Pose. The motion (*mtn) file loads according to the settings. Save Motion Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Joint Motion The Save File window appears. Type in file name and designate the path the file will be saved to. The Motion (*mtn) file will be saved to the designated path. Note: Motion files can only be saved when imported as Avatars in COLLADA format with Motion Data, and the COLLADA files must be in Open COLLADA format. To learn more about COLLADA format, please reference 3D File (COLLADA) Import. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions.

Title: 1:N Segment Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. Note The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user. While establishing 1:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the sewing line cannot be applied. While establishing N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: Technical guidance for TLS 1.2 update
Content: What is TLS (Transport Layer Security)? Transport Layer Security is a security protocol designed to facilitate data security for communications on the Internet. It protects users' data from various cyber threats and provides a secure connection between users by encrypting data. Does TLS update affect my use of software? Since this update applies to the server, there is no direct impact on users and software. All Operating Systems released after Windows 8 and macOS 10.9 have supported TLS 1.2 by default, so users of the latest OS can seamlessly use the software. Please check if your OS meets the system requirements here. How can I get help? If you encounter any of the following problems during the startup and login, please contact us with a screenshot and detailed description. An error message "Delayed Network Connection" displays when login software. Login window does not appear. Software does not respond after login attempt. Read more When the OS is updated to the latest, various problems caused by differences in TLS versions can be prevented in advance. Find out how to update your OS on the Microsoft or Apple website. This document provides technical guidance for the server and software. For TLS-related problems from your web browser or the specific website you are accessing, please contact the appropriate provider.

Title: Slash & Spread
Content: Objective Slash and spread a Pattern using an Internal Line inside the Pattern (ver2.4.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Operation Slash &amp Spread Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, Click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). Choose the side of the Pattern to be rotated. The selected side of the Pattern is highlighted in yellow. Drag the mouse cursor towards the Pattern should be rotated. The preview of the edited pattern appears. When the desired shape is achieved, click on the 2D window to complete Slash &amp Spread. Slash &amp Spread with Distance and Angle Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Slash &amp Spread 2D Toolbar Slash &amp Spread Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). Right click on the 2D window to access the pop-up menu. The Spread window appears. Enter the desired values for Distance and Angle. Distance Set how much in length the selected side of the Pattern spreads. Angle Set the angle the selected side of the Pattern spreads. Click OK to complete Slash &amp Spread. Note: When selecting an Internal Line as a Slash Line, the side closer to the mouse cursor spreads. Click on the slash line to spread patterns on both sides. (ver MD10) The shape of the Pattern can be previewed when closing the Pattern. Also, the Pattern Outline is smoothened into a natural curve. (ver MD10)

Title: Add Perpendicular Internal Line
Content: Objective Create Internal Lines perpendicular to Pattern outlines or 2D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Add from a Point Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the point of a Pattern outline or Internal Line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Hover the mouse over the Add Perpendicular Internal Line option. Below options appear. X-Axis Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's X-axis. Y-Axis Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's Y-axis. Local Can type in Internal Line's angle based on the selected segment. Select the desired option. The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window with different options appears based on your selection. Option Description X-Axis/ Y-Axis Local (Pattern outline) Local (Internal Line) Angle Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length Type in Internal Line's length. Extend When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Opposite Segment Not Applicable Internal Line is created based on the other side of the selected line. Reverse Not Applicable The Internal Line is reversed. Add from a Segment Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Add Perpendicular Internal Line. The Internal Line preview appears at the center of the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line. The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. Configure below options as needed and click OK. Option Description Angle Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length Type in the length of the Internal Line. Distance to Segment Edge Locate the Internal Line. The Internal Line preview shifts as number changes. Extend When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Reverse The Internal Line is reversed. The Internal Line is created accordingly.

Title: 3D M:N Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Note: 3D Sewing Video

Content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. Title: Coupon Guideline
Content: QUESTION 1. How do I apply a coupon code received from the Marvelous Designer Team? 2. How can I redeem a coupon issued for my account? ANSWER To apply a coupon code: Step 1. Log in to our website using your Personal ID. Step 2. Go to "My Account" at https://marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/account. Step 3. Click on "Coupon List". Step 4. Enter your code and save it. Step 5. The coupon code will now be available in the list, and you can click on "Apply." *Depending on the coupon type, you will be directed to the checkout process or you will be able to redeem the coupon immediately. ANSWER To redeem a coupon issued for your account: Step 1. Log in to our website using your Personal ID. Step 2. Go to "My Account" at https://marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/account. Step 3. Click on "Coupon List". Step 4. If the coupon is available, you will be able to apply it. Title: Mirror Paste Buttonhole
Content: Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. Note: Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.

Title: Create Buttons along Pattern Outline
Content: Objective Create buttons along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. Location Main Menu Materials Button Button 3D toolbar Button Operation Create Select the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the outline of the pattern. The button/buttonhole creation option window appears along the pattern outline. Note: Hold down the Shift key and left-click on a segment to select multiple. Set each option and click OK. Type Start Position Repeatedly create a button based on the starting point. Distribute Create by aligning buttons at regular intervals between the starting and ending points. Based on Start Start Position Distance Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and the center of the button. Interval Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the button. Reverse The starting point of the button and replicated created direction are adjusted in reverse. Replicate Interval Adjust the distance between the buttons. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Adjust the number of buttons. Distribute (ver. 11) Position Distance Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and t he center of the button. Start/End Interval Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the start/end buttons. Replicate Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Enter the number of buttons/buttonholes to align between the start and end points. A group button is created. Select Select the tool/menu indicated. Click a button or segment created along the pattern outline. All grouped buttons are selected. Change the button properties and style or right-click. Applied to grouped buttons. Group information is not copied/pasted. Note: If clicking again on the selected group button, it is able to select a button individually. Grouped buttons cannot be moved. Unlink Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. After right-clicking on a button or segment created along the pattern outline and click Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. The group is unlinked.

Note: From ver2.5.0, the location of the Bind Position has been moved from the Buttonhole Style Properties to an individual property. Therefore it is now available to edit individual buttons and buttonholes. 2D Measurement View the position of buttonholes in 2D pattern with its size measurement. Set check-boxes On for Left/Right/Up/Down as desired. The 2D size measurements appear accordingly.

Title: Move Buttonhole
Content: Objective Move buttonholes as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Move Buttonholes with Click-and-Drag Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Click and drag the buttonholes to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. Title: Copy/Paste Buttonhole
Content: Objective Copy and paste multiple buttonholes with keeping the interval space evenly. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Copy/Paste Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Pase Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. The Paste window appears. Input desired value for interval/number of buttonholes/position. Interval Sets the distance between buttonholes. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Sets the number of buttonholes to copy/paste. The buttonholes are now being created and applied accordingly.
